messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Patel <sam.patel@acmehealth.com>, Laura Chen <l.chen@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>

Subject: Follow-up: GDPR / DPA / SCC modules — post-call recap and next steps

Hi Sam + Laura —

Thanks again for the call earlier — great to hear more about Acme Health's rollout plans and data flows. Quick recap and proposed next steps so your legal/procurement teams have everything in one place: 

Call recap:
- Scope: Redwood will provide hosted inference for Acme Health's patient-facing triage assistant.
- Data types discussed: PII (name, email), limited clinical notes (de-identified except where necessary), and metadata.
- Expected volume: ~2M tokens/month initially.

Immediate next steps (we can move in parallel):
1) DPA: I attached a draft DPA for your legal to review (Redwood_DPA_Draft_v1.pdf). We typically sign a Controller-Processor DPA for this use case.
2) SCCs: Based on how you described the integration (Redwood processing data on behalf of Acme), we recommend Module Two (Controller-to-Processor) of the EU Standard Contractual Clauses. Neha from our security/compliance team is cc'd and will confirm.
3) SOC 2 & evidence: Attached is a high-level SOC 2 summary (SOC2_summary.pdf). We can provide the full report under NDA or via our secure portal.
4) Vendor security questionnaire: If you have a questionnaire, please send it over and we’ll complete it. Alternatively, we have a short vendor intake doc we can fill — link: https://app.redwood.ai/security/questionnaire/ACME-045
5) Timeline: If your legal can review the DPA this week, we can turn around redlines within 2-3 business days.

Attachments: Redwood_DPA_Draft_v1.pdf (draft), SOC2_summary.pdf

Proposal: If this looks right, could you confirm:
- That Acme intends to treat Redwood as a Processor for this integration?
- Who on your legal/procurement side should we include on DPA/SCC discussions?

I’ll set up a short follow-up with Rishi + Neha to walk through the DPA and SCC selection if helpful.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales Lead | Redwood Inference

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the quick recap and for sending the DPA. A couple questions from our legal side before we kick off the redline: 

1) Role confirmation — can you confirm in writing that Redwood will act as a Processor (not Controller) for the triage assistant? We want that explicit in the DPA and SCC selection.
2) SCC module — you mentioned Module Two; is that the recommended baseline for cross-border transfers to the US? Any additional modules/UK addendum we should expect?

4) Questionnaire — we have a vendor security questionnaire (attached). Can you confirm who will complete it and estimated turnaround?

Laura is our counsel and will lead the DPA review. I’m looping her on next steps. We’d like to get a signed DPA + SCCs in place before starting the pilot.

Best,

Hi Sam + Laura —

Thanks — answers inline below and next steps: 

1) Role confirmation: Confirmed — Redwood will be a Processor for the triage assistant (processing strictly on behalf of Acme per the integration described). We’ll include explicit language in the DPA.

2) SCC module: For controller -> processor relationship, Module Two (Controller to Processor) of the EU SCCs is the standard choice. If you have UK transfers, we typically add the UK Addendum. Neha will confirm and can provide a short guidance note.

3) Customization: We’re open to limited, commercially reasonable redlines around breach timelines and deletion windows; we aim to be responsive on routine DPA redlines (our usual turnaround is 2-3 business days after receiving counsel comments). For subprocessors we provide a current list and a 30-day notification for additions.

4) Questionnaire: Thanks — I received Acme_Vendor_Security_Questionnaire.xlsx. Could you please confirm if you want us to fill it out directly or if you prefer a short questionnaire response + SOC2 evidence via secure portal? Either way, Rishi will coordinate completion. We typically return vendor questionnaires within 3-5 business days.

Next steps:
- I’ll ask Neha to provide SCC module guidance (short doc attached).
- We’ll upload the SOC2 report to the secure portal and share access once we have an NDA if required.
- Please let us know who on procurement/legal will own the redline thread.

Subject: Re: Follow-up: GDPR / DPA / SCC modules — post-call guidance from security/compliance

Hi Laura + Sam —

Thanks for the detailed questions — happy to provide guidance and a recommended path to minimize legal friction. Key points below: 

1) Role clarification (Controller vs Processor)
- Based on the integration notes (Acme sends patient data to Redwood for inference; Acme controls the purpose and means), Redwood is a Processor. We will accept a Controller-to-Processor DPA. Please ensure the DPA includes the scope of processing and retention windows.

2) SCC module selection
- Recommendation: EU SCCs Module Two (Controller -> Processor). This covers transfers from Acme (controller) to Redwood (processor).
- If transfers will go to the UK, include the UK Addendum. If Acme insists on additional protections, Module One (Controller -> Controller) is not appropriate for this architecture.

3) Subprocessors and notice
- We maintain a subprocessors list; current major subprocessors are: AWS (us-east-1, eu-west-1), S3 storage, and our telemetry provider. We provide a rolling list at https://app.redwood.ai/subprocessors and 30 days notice for new subprocessors.

4) Data subject rights & deletion
- Standard: We will delete customer data per contract terms; typical options are: 30/90/180 days post-termination. Please indicate your preferred retention period in the DPA redline.

5) SOC 2 and evidence
- Full SOC 2 Type II is available under NDA. We can also provide a redacted executive summary immediately (already shared).

6) Timeline & next steps
- If Acme provides redline comments by EOD Thu (PST), we can respond to DPA comments within 2 business days.
- For the questionnaire, if you upload it to our portal (link below), we’ll complete within 3 business days.

Attachments: SCC_selection_guidance.docx (short guidance)

Portal & evidence links:
- Security intake: https://app.redwood.ai/security/questionnaire/ACME-045
- Subprocessors list: https://app.redwood.ai/subprocessors

Happy to set a quick (30m) call with Laura + Acme legal to walk through the DPA and SCC selection if that would help speed alignment.

Regards,
Neha Kapoor
Security & Compliance Manager | Redwood Inference
